Hi there, and good evening, everyone! Today is Saturday, November 14, 2026. Welcome to Goodnight Coffee. I’m your host, An’an! Tonight, let’s talk about the freshest, piping-hot business and tech updates—relaxed, engaging, and packed with insight. So put on your headphones and let’s get tonight’s show started!

@@@

According to QbitAI, Nvidia has announced that Jensen Huang has resigned as the company’s president, CEO, and director, effective immediately. Colette Kress, currently executive vice president and CFO, will serve as interim CEO while retaining her current role until a permanent successor is appointed. After the news broke, Nvidia shares in premarket trading fell as low as $150.13, down about 13.58% from the previous close; after the open, the decline remained above 10%, before narrowing to 4.63% by press time. Jensen Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and led the company for 33 years. The board has launched a formal CEO search and will consider both internal and external candidates; it has also appointed Harvey C. Jones as the first board chair in the company’s history. He previously served as CEO and executive chairman of Synopsys. Kress has been with Nvidia for more than 13 years, and the announcement said she has played a key role in the company’s growth and transformation. On January 27, 2025, when DeepSeek triggered a reassessment of AI compute spending, Nvidia fell about 17% in a single day and lost roughly $593 billion in market value—at the time the largest single-day market-value loss for a U.S. company. The board expects the company’s operations, customer commitments, and product roadmap to continue as planned, and it will report third-quarter fiscal 2027 results and hold its earnings call on November 17 as scheduled.

@@@

According to Huxiu 24 Hours, OpenAI has disbanded its standalone robotics team and is instead betting on general-purpose large models.

@@@

According to Sina Tech, SpaceX completed the 15th test flight of Starship on Friday but failed to recover either of the two stages. The rocket lifted off from a launch site in southern Texas at 4:47 p.m. local time, 5:47 p.m. Eastern. This was the most ambitious Starship mission to date, with the company attempting for the first time to catch both the booster and the upper stage. After the booster catch was called off, it made a controlled splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico and caught fire on the water. Earlier that day, SpaceX received a launch license from the Federal Aviation Administration. Hours later, the agency issued a nationwide ground stop due to communications failures at multiple air traffic control centers, but said the license was unaffected. After the booster catch failed, the upper stage continued along its planned trajectory, with plans to orbit Earth 14 times and, if all went well, land at Starbase on Saturday. SpaceX said the mission deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites; its constellation already has more than 11,000 active low-Earth-orbit satellites. A single Starship can carry up to 60 V3 satellites, with roughly 20 times the capacity of Falcon 9, aiming for Starlink to carry 51% of global internet traffic. William Blair analysts said that even with the failed catch this time, a delay of a few months would have limited impact. In addition, Zelensky said Ukraine’s military Starshield service was again restricted without warning, and several U.S. senators condemned the move and called for a congressional investigation.

@@@

According to Sina Tech, Microsoft is gradually recovering from an outage that lasted all day. The disruption began on Thursday and initially affected only the U.S. and the Americas, but as engineers struggled to restore downed servers, the problem quickly spread worldwide. It grew from outages in Outlook email and Teams video meetings to personal and enterprise cloud services such as email, file storage, and document storage. Copilot AI tools, Defender security software, and the Intune management console were also down for a time, and some users reported being unable to access cloud Windows virtual machines. Microsoft has not announced a root cause, saying only that the incident involved “a large number of servers unexpectedly unavailable,” and that the investigation is ongoing. By Friday morning on the U.S. East Coast, Outlook began to recover and some emails started arriving. Doug Madory, director of internet analysis at Kentik, said that after about 18 hours of downtime, traffic to Microsoft’s services began to recover. In a Friday status update, Microsoft said there was no evidence that the incident was related to a malicious attack. When media asked whether Microsoft had logs or other technical means to detect malicious activity and whether it could reconstruct the incident, its spokesperson had not yet responded. The last major Microsoft cloud outage occurred in September, which Microsoft attributed to a “core identity authentication configuration issue” that prevented users from signing in to services.

@@@

According to 36Kr, on November 12, Google released Gemini 4 Hydrogen and rolled it out globally, replacing Gemini 3.8 Flash as the series’ “efficiency execution layer.” It launched fully the same day across the Gemini app, API, enterprise edition, and Antigravity; Search AI Mode made it the default model. Artificial Analysis shows that its default high setting scores 51, surpassing the flagship Argon’s 50; compared with 3.8 Flash, it is 2.5 times faster, Terminal-Bench 4.1 rises from 18.2% to 57%, and hallucinations are reduced by more than fivefold. API pricing is $1.5 per million input tokens and $7.5 per million output tokens. The Orchestrator can switch between Carbon and Hydrogen within the same session; Google says this saves 24% of quota and is 19% faster. This is the third Gemini 4 model in six weeks. Its price is double that of 3.8 Flash, and the new pricing will apply uniformly after the old promotional pricing ends on December 31.

@@@

According to TechWeb, on November 14, DeepSeek released its “full-suite” application API, packaging the complete set of mature interaction capabilities from its own app into standardized modules for developers. Unlike previous offerings that only provided model inference interfaces, this release covers application-layer capabilities such as search, web crawling and parsing, file parsing, OCR, speech recognition, and speech synthesis, which can be called individually or embedded in combination into workflows. By enabling the corresponding parameters in the existing API, developers can get conversational features such as deep-thinking search and file input, with tool calls and context assembly handled automatically on the server side. Currently, the V4.1-Flash model, deepseek-flash, supports web search, deep-thinking search, file input, link reading, and model safety in the Messages, Responses, and Chat Completions interfaces. Web search can automatically initiate webpage or image searches and answer with citations; deep-thinking search can independently go online to read links during multi-step reasoning; file input supports parsing formats such as PDF, Office, and images; and safety checks can review model inputs and outputs and return refusal markers for risks. Capabilities such as Search, Fetch, OCR, ASR, and TTS can also be called independently. DeepSeek said that in addition to token fees, it will charge tool-call fees for the extended capabilities; those providing application services externally must enable safety parameters and assume obligations such as content safety review, large-model registration, and AI labeling.

@@@

According to Readhub, Moonshot AI, the developer of the Kimi large model, is considering an IPO in Hong Kong as early as early 2027 and has begun dismantling its overseas holding structure to pave the way. The restructuring path is as follows: first, the company will repurchase overseas shares from U.S. dollar-denominated shareholders, then arrange for the relevant funds to be invested in the domestic entity. Previously, Moonshot AI completed its final private funding round at a valuation of about $50 billion; the company is considering raising up to $5 billion in the IPO and has confidentially submitted a listing application to the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. Moonshot AI said it does not comment on market rumors or speculation. The company was founded by Yang Zhilin and focuses on the Kimi series of large models. If it completes a listing at a $50 billion valuation, it would be one of the largest IPOs among Chinese large-model companies.

@@@

According to Readhub, China’s 2026 national medical insurance drug catalog and commercial insurance innovative drug catalog were announced. A total of two innovative drugs were transferred from the first commercial insurance innovative drug catalog into basic medical insurance, further deepening the coordination and linkage between the two catalogs. Among them, JW Therapeutics’ relma-cel injection was included in basic medical insurance for the first time. It is a million-yuan-class CAR-T cancer therapy, and after medical insurance reimbursement, patients’ out-of-pocket costs can fall to under 100,000 yuan. The core reason the drug entered basic medical insurance with a significant price cut is that key raw materials have been localized, greatly reducing production costs.

According to cnBeta, China’s 10-ton-class electric commercial aircraft CE-25A has successfully completed its first piloted flight.

item.title: 《晚安咖啡》科技夜话：黄仁勋辞任英伟达CEO，微软云服务全球宕机，谷歌发布Gemini 4 Hydrogen
item.description:
嗨~~大家晚上好呀！今天是2026年11月14日，星期六，欢迎来到《晚安咖啡》，我是主播安安！今天咱们一起聊聊新鲜热乎的商业科技动态，轻松又有料，快戴上耳机，和我一起开启今晚的分享吧！

@@@

据量子位消息，英伟达宣布黄仁勋已辞去公司总裁、首席执行官及董事职务，即刻生效。现任执行副总裁兼CFO Colette Kress出任临时CEO，并继续兼任原职，直至正式继任者获任命。消息公布后，英伟达盘前股价一度跌至150.13美元，较前一交易日收盘下跌约13.58%；开盘后跌幅仍超10%，发稿前收窄至4.63%。黄仁勋1993年联合创办英伟达，掌舵33年。董事会已启动正式CEO遴选，将同时考虑内外候选人；并任命Harvey C. Jones为公司历史上首位董事会主席，他曾任新思科技CEO和执行董事长。Kress在英伟达工作超过13年，公告称她在公司增长与转型中发挥关键作用。2025年1月27日DeepSeek引发AI算力投入重估时，英伟达曾单日收跌约17%，市值蒸发约5930亿美元，创当时美股单家公司单日市值损失纪录。董事会预计公司运营、客户承诺及产品路线图将继续推进，并按原定安排于11月17日公布2027财年第三季度业绩、召开财报电话会议。

@@@

据虎嗅24小时消息，OpenAI已解散独立机器人团队，转而押注通用大模型。

@@@

新浪科技消息，SpaceX周五完成星舰第15次试飞，但未能回收两级箭体。火箭于当地时间下午4时47分（美国东部时间下午5时47分）从得州南部发射场升空。此次是迄今目标最高的星舰任务，公司首次尝试同时捕获助推器与上面级；助推器捕获取消后受控溅落墨西哥湾，并在海面起火。当天早些时候SpaceX获美国联邦航空管理局发射许可，数小时后该局因多个空管中心通信故障发布全国停飞指令，但称该许可未受影响。助推器捕获失败后，上面级继续沿预定轨道飞行，计划环绕地球14圈，若顺利周六降落在星基地发射场。SpaceX称本次释放26颗星链V3卫星；其星座已有超过11000颗在轨活跃低轨卫星，一枚星舰最多可搭载60颗V3卫星，运力约为猎鹰9号20倍，目标是让星链承载全球51%互联网流量。威廉·布莱尔分析师称，即便本次捕获失败，推迟数月影响有限。此外，泽连斯基称乌军星盾服务再遭无预警限制，多名美国参议员谴责并呼吁国会调查。

@@@

据新浪科技报道，微软正从持续一整天的服务中断中逐步恢复。故障始于周四，最初仅影响美国及美洲区域，但因工程师难以恢复宕机服务器，问题很快蔓延至全球；影响从Outlook邮件、Teams视频会议无法使用，扩大到邮件、文件、文档存储等个人与企业云服务，Copilot AI工具、Defender安全检测软件及Intune管理控制台也一度瘫痪，另有用户反馈云Windows虚拟机无法访问。微软尚未公布根因，仅称事故是“大量服务器意外不可用”，调查仍在推进。美国东海岸周五上午，Outlook开始恢复，部分邮件陆续送达；Kentik互联网分析总监道格·马多里称，经过约18小时停机后，微软各项服务流量开始回升。微软在周五状态公告中表示，暂无证据表明事件与恶意攻击有关。媒体询问微软是否具备日志等技术手段侦测恶意行为、能否复盘事故经过，其发言人暂未回应。上一次微软大规模云服务事故发生在9月，微软归因于“核心身份验证配置问题”，导致用户无法登录服务。

@@@

据36氪报道，11月12日谷歌发布Gemini 4 Hydrogen并全球推送，接替Gemini 3.8 Flash成为系列“效率执行层”。它当天在Gemini应用、API、企业版和Antigravity等全量上线；搜索AI Mode将其设为默认模型。Artificial Analysis显示，其默认high档51分，超过旗舰Argon的50分；相较3.8 Flash，速度快2.5倍，Terminal-Bench 4.1从18.2%升至57%，幻觉降低5倍以上。API定价每百万输入/输出1.5/7.5美元。Orchestrator可在同一会话切换Carbon与Hydrogen，谷歌称省24%配额、快19%。这是六周内第三款Gemini 4，其价格较3.8 Flash翻倍，旧优惠价12月31日结束后统一新价。

TechWeb消息，11月14日，DeepSeek发布“全家桶”应用API，将自有App中已成熟的整套交互能力打包为标准化模块向开发者开放。与以往仅提供模型推理接口不同，此次覆盖搜索、网页抓取与解析、文件解析、OCR、语音识别、语音合成等应用层能力，支持单独调用或组合嵌入工作流。开发者在原有API中开启对应参数，即可获得深度思考搜索、文件输入等对话功能，工具调用与上下文拼接由服务端自动完成。目前，V4.1-Flash模型（deepseek-flash）已在Messages、Responses和Chat Completions接口支持联网搜索、深度思考搜索、文件输入、阅读链接及模型安全；联网搜索可自动发起网页或图片搜索并附引用作答，深度思考搜索可在多步推理中自主联网阅读链接，文件输入支持PDF、Office、图片等格式解析，安全校验可审核模型输入输出并对风险返回拒答标识。Search、Fetch、OCR、ASR、TTS等能力也可独立调用。DeepSeek表示，扩展能力除Token费用外还将收取工具调用费用；对外提供应用服务须开启安全参数，并承担内容安全审核、大模型登记、AI标识等义务。

据Readhub报道，Kimi大模型开发商月之暗面正考虑最早于2027年初在香港上市，并已着手拆除海外控股架构，为IPO铺路。相关重组路径为：先由公司从美元股东手中回购海外股份，再安排相关资金投资境内主体。此前，月之暗面已完成最后一轮私募融资，估值约500亿美元；公司正考虑在IPO中募资最多50亿美元，并已以保密形式向港交所递交上市申请。月之暗面方面表示，不对市场传言或猜测置评。该公司由杨植麟创立，主推Kimi系列大模型。若按500亿美元估值完成上市，这将成为中国大模型公司中规模最大的IPO之一。

item.description:
Hi~~ good evening, everyone! It's Friday, November 13, 2026. I'm An'an, your host at Goodnight Coffee, and I'm super happy to be with you again! Today I've got a fresh batch of business and tech updates—plenty of substance, easy to follow. Let's jump right into today's show!

@@@

According to CNBC, Nvidia is nearing its longest weekly losing streak since 2012. As of Thursday's close, the stock had fallen 11% this week and 4.3% on Thursday, on track for a sixth consecutive weekly decline. In this round, its market value has shrunk by 29%, or about $1.6 trillion, and it has fallen below Apple. On the same day, the board announced that co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang had resigned, appointed CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO, and is searching for a successor. Earlier, two extramarital affairs involving Huang had been made public: one involved a person alleged to be a Chinese spy, and the other involved the company's vice president of its healthcare business. He wrote to employees over the weekend apologizing for being "unfaithful to his wife." Before Huang's departure last week, Nvidia shares had already fallen about 9%; after the midterm elections, a decisive Democratic victory and the passage of several ballot measures that could slow AI construction deepened the selloff. Nvidia plans to report quarterly results next Tuesday, with analysts expecting revenue to rise 91% year on year to $108.9 billion, 18 times the same period in 2022. Oppenheimer said Huang's departure could create a persistent share overhang, while D.A. Davidson cut its price target from $300 to $200.

@@@

According to The Verge, Microsoft's Outlook email service has still not recovered. Since early Thursday afternoon, users in many parts of the world have reported being unable to access Outlook mailboxes via the web or the app. Microsoft later acknowledged the issue on its Microsoft 365 Status account, saying some infrastructure was experiencing elevated load in multiple regions, which could cause connection errors; Teams also had reports of problems, though less severe. Microsoft said the impact involves the Microsoft 365 commercial service suite, mainly Exchange Online, and that some users may be unable to access mailboxes, with email delivery possibly delayed. Microsoft Communications Director Ben Hope said the company was aware of the issue and investigating, thanked customers for their patience, and would restore service as soon as possible. Several hours later, Microsoft updated its progress multiple times, saying it was encountering difficulties restarting servers and monitoring server health. By about 6 p.m. Eastern Time, Microsoft said it had restored service to some affected servers, which were currently stable, and had shifted traffic and connections to alternate paths, with limited recovery in some regions. The company also simplified the recovery process and implemented protective traffic management at specific locations to reduce load; if the results are positive, it will expand the measure to more locations. However, there is still no timeline for full recovery.

@@@

According to VentureBeat, China-linked hackers implanted backdoors into executives' laptops via USB, exploiting a vulnerability targeted by a fix that companies already had but had not deployed. The report says the fix already existed, but the company involved had not enabled it, allowing attackers to breach executives' devices.

@@@

According to cnBeta, Mercedes-Benz is pausing all investment in its German plants and considering closing some factories to cope with high vehicle manufacturing costs. The investment pause follows a failure to reach consensus with the works council and union representatives on cutting labor costs. Production chief Michael Schiebe said management had jointly decided to halt follow-up investment at German sites. In September, he warned that two German plants could close if there was no progress; Thursday's information indicates that management is preparing for possible closures. Management board member Britta Seeger said in an employee memo that she wants to avoid closures at all costs, but the option must be discussed further. Negotiations between the company and the IG Metall union are still underway. The crisis in Germany's auto industry is escalating: Volkswagen Group previously carried out its largest restructuring ever, threatening tens of thousands of jobs; Schaeffler announced last week that, hit by weak demand for combustion-engine vehicles, it plans to cut 3,460 jobs in Europe and close five facilities, four of them in Germany. Analyst Dudenhöffer said this is not surprising; unless the cost structure is thoroughly reformed, the industry's future is at risk.

@@@

According to TechWeb, JD.com announced on the evening of November 12 that it had completed its takeover offer for German consumer electronics retail group CECONOMY. Through a wholly owned indirect subsidiary, it acquired 59.8% of the share capital and voting rights for €4.60 per share in cash, with total consideration of €1.335 billion. CECONOMY has become a JD subsidiary, and its results will be consolidated into JD's financial statements from November 12, 2026; together with the 25.3% stake retained by partner Convergenta, the two sides hold a combined 85.2%. Merger control, foreign investment, and EU foreign subsidy approvals have all been completed. CECONOMY operates more than 1,000 stores in 11 European markets under the MediaMarkt, Saturn, and MediaWorld brands, employs more than 50,000 people, and had more than 53 million loyalty members in 2025. The announcement said CECONOMY will maintain independent operations and its local technology architecture, with no plans to adjust staffing, employee agreements, or office locations. JD CEO Xu Ran said the two sides will build a leading next-generation consumer electronics platform in Europe; CECONOMY CEO Remko Rijnders said the partnership is now in place and implementation is moving forward.

@@@

According to TechWeb, after news of organizational changes and personnel adjustments emerged from Tencent's internal all-hands meeting marking its 28th anniversary, rumors that "Tencent will lay off 50% of staff" appeared on social platforms. On November 12, Tencent PR Director Zhang Jun denied the rumors on Weibo, calling them "nothing but a misunderstanding and rumor." A Tencent insider said it was a summary of an internal speech, not an internal document, and that management hopes businesses that have not yet been mobilized will get moving. On November 11, Tencent's core executives held their regular online dialogue with all employees, with Ma Huateng and Liu Chiping speaking. The leaked speech shows Ma Huateng used the analogy of "shifting from land warfare to naval warfare," called the current situation "a life-or-death transformation," and urged employees to shed complacency and respond with agility. He said the AI shock has arrived and that the company must prepare new playbooks and get on board. Tencent is taking on heavy-asset businesses for the first time. Around 2021, cost reduction and efficiency improvement had already escalated into a deep organizational restructuring; the goal is not to cut costs but to adapt to a new battlefield, and the hope is to let small teams do big things with existing headcount. He proposed that for traditional core businesses, half the people should defend and half should fight new campaigns; on staffing, the company must decisively choose people who can adapt to the new playbook, and stop coaxing people or negotiating conditions before they get on board. Ma Huateng concluded that this LinkTime was intentionally stricter than in the past.

@@@

According to 36Kr, Unitree Robotics' share price, after halving two months ago, rebounded; as of November 11, it had doubled in less than a month, and its market cap returned to RMB 300 billion. JPMorgan upgraded its rating two notches from "underweight" to "overweight." On October 22, Wang Xingxing judged that physical AI had begun to show signs of a breakthrough, with a window that could arrive in the next one to two years, or two to three years; JPMorgan subsequently raised its 2028 humanoid robot shipment forecast from about 41,600 units to 111,600 units. On November 4, an Apple research team published HALO results: Unitree G1 was tested 360 times across six unfamiliar environments for six categories of individual skills, achieving an average success rate of 91% on individual tasks. None of these environments were used in training or pre-scanned for mapping; training used data generated from about 1,000 virtual environments. The base version of Unitree G1 now starts at RMB 85,000, down from RMB 99,000; after the 2025 price cut, the overall gross margin remained 63.18%. In 2025, Unitree shipped 5,511 humanoid robots, more than ten times the previous year; in October this year, Wang Xingxing disclosed that cumulative production of the G1 had reached about 10,000 to 20,000 units. In the first three quarters of this year, R&D investment was RMB 263 million, up 191.48% year on year, higher than the 55.71% revenue growth in the same period.

@@@

According to Sina Tech, DJI's official website published a notice on November 13 regarding suggested retail price adjustments for some products, saying that due to the sustained sharp rise in costs of multiple key components, including global semiconductors and memory, and after careful evaluation, DJI will adjust the suggested retail prices of some products from midnight on November 18, 2026. Previously, social media rumors said that DJI Pocket 4, Pocket 4P, and the entire Nano series would see across-the-board price increases starting November 18, with increases of up to 13% and up to RMB 500 per unit.

@@@

According to Sina Tech, on the evening of November 12, a full-featured integrated innovative terminal jointly developed and promoted by China UnionPay and Ant Group made its national debut at Intime Commercial's Xi'an Bell Tower Kaiyuan Mall. It is authorized for distribution and operation by UnionPay Merchant Services. The terminal can accept major payment methods on one device, including Alipay's "Tap!", domestic and international bank cards, aggregated QR code payments, mobile Pay, and digital RMB. It is currently the most comprehensive financial-grade smart POS terminal on the market in terms of payment method compatibility, meeting requirements such as UnionPay enterprise technical specifications and Alipay IoT device security specifications. The new device also offers value-added digital operation capabilities such as AI business analysis, intelligent customer-flow analysis, precision member operations, and government consumption-promotion programs. Intime Commercial's Xi'an Bell Tower Kaiyuan Mall is the first national chain high-end mall to deploy it, and will be among the first to offer services such as member recognition, payment settlement, and voice-reminder shopping guidance. China UnionPay Chairman Dong Junfeng said this is the industry's first innovative device to achieve integrated payment acceptance; Ant Group CEO Han Xinyi said the new device is fully compatible with various payment methods, and the two sides will continue to deepen cooperation. Since Alipay launched "Tap!" in July 2024, the service has covered 2,200 segmented scenarios such as food ordering and transportation, connected 30 million offline locations, and served 400 million users.

@@@

All right, that's all for today's show! Thank you for spending time with us—and remember to take your good mood with you! If you enjoy our program, you're very welcome to subscribe and share it with your friends; it really helps us. See you next time!
